title: Pinning: telemetry-driven routing patterns (exploratory)
content:
Purpose: quick exploration of using runtime telemetry to drive routing decisions when model versions are pinned. Goal is to define practical heuristics that balance strict pin guarantees with availability, latency, and cost objectives across regions and Dedicated/Private fleets. This is intentionally exploratory — concrete rules and safety checks needed before any rollout.

Background/context:
- We currently support explicit model version pinning (customer/route-level). Pinning ensures deterministic outputs for app owners but complicates routing: pinned version may not be available in every region or capacity tier.
- Control plane already maintains a registry of model artifacts and variant metadata (quantized variants, ops dependencies, tokenizer hashes). The registry indicates compatibility tags but we lack a compact scoring function that the routing layer can use in real time.
- Telemetry available at request time and aggregated: per-route latency/percentiles, per-model token cost, per-variant error rates, availability per region, queue length, per-GPU utilization, and cache/kvc hit ratios.

High-level idea:
Use a telemetry-informed compatibility and cost score to rank candidate servers/regions for a pinned request. Score = compatibility_penalty + latency_penalty + availability_bonus + cost_penalty + regulatory_penalty. Smallest score wins. Penalties are tunable and derived from real-time signals and registry metadata.

Design constraints and non-goals:
- Non-goal: allow arbitrary violation of pin guarantees for correctness-sensitive customers. For those customers we must preserve strict pinning or require manual opt-in for fallbacks.
- Must be conservative: first rollout should only apply relaxed pinning for read-only inference workloads where slight model differences are acceptable.
- Must be auditable and reversible per-customer. All fallback decisions logged and surfaced in console.

Registry metadata we should surface to routing (suggested fields):
- artifact_id (string): unique model+version identifier
- tokenizer_hash (string)
- kv_cache_compat (boolean or enum: exact/compatible/incompatible)
- op_vector (list of op ids or fingerprint)
- quantization_profile (e.g., fp16, int8-llm, int4)
- region_availability (list of regions with variant present)
- guaranteed_semantics (flag: deterministic|non-deterministic|sensitive)

Compatibility scoring sketch (numeric heuristics):
- tokenizer_mismatch => +1000 (hard barrier for strict mode; in relaxed mode +50)
- kv_cache_incompatible => +300 (if request uses prefix caching; heavy penalty)
- op_vector_missing_ops => +500 per missing op (can't run on device)
- quantization_variant_mismatch => +30 for small ops, +200 if known to degrade quality for workload

Telemetry-informed components (real-time):
- observed_p50_latency_region (ms) relative to SLO => latency_penalty = (observed_p50 - SLO_ms) * alpha
- region_availability_score = fraction_of_healthy_nodes * 100
- recent_error_rate (5m) => availability_bonus negative if high errors
- cost_per_token_estimate => adds to cost_penalty (used for routing toward cheaper quantized variant)

Routing modes (proposed):
1) Strict pin: only route to endpoints that match artifact_id exactly. For missing region capacity, failover only to same region replicas of exact artifact. No telemetry overrides.
2) Preferred pin (default for many routes): prefer exact artifact; if unavailable, evaluate compatible variants with score threshold. Allows quantized-compatible or minor tokeniser variant if compatibility score < X. Log and surface in console and email when fallback triggered.
3) Relaxed pin (opt-in): allow routing to best-effort variant that matches high-level semantics (e.g., same model family + tokenizer) with penalties; targeted for experimental or low-risk routes.

Multi-region specifics:
- Geo-preference: customers can opt to prefer region-local instances. By default we prefer lower-latency region even if variant is quantized (score tradeoff).
- Cross-region failover rule: if local region p99 latency > SLO * 1.5 OR local region availability < 80% for 2 consecutive minutes, allow cross-region evaluation.
- Data residency: if route has residency flag, only allow regions listed in registry metadata; residency overrides latency/cost tradeoffs.

Control plane responsibilities:
- Maintain an up-to-date compatibility snapshot that's cheap to fetch: registry publishes small compatibility vectors per artifact for routing agents in edge proxies.
- Periodic reconciliation job that marks artifacts stale when their ops/quant profiles change (so routing agents get notified).
- Expose an API to evaluate candidate list and return ranked decisions for observability/testing (not mandatory for the router to call synchronously).

Telemetry instrumentation required (short list):
- Mark requests that experienced a fallback from pin to variant (fallback_reason, source_artifact, chosen_variant)
- Per-variant quality regressions: tie eval prompts (a small set) to production responses to catch regressions early.
- Add per-route control-plane events: pin-change, registry-update, rollout-start/complete.

Simulation / canary strategy:
1) Offline simulation: replay last 7 days of routing decisions with synthetic variant availability graphs and compute expected SLO changes and approximate quality deltas. Metric outputs: %requests that would have needed fallback, median latency change, estimated cost delta, number of customers impacted.
2) Canary routing agents in a single non-critical region: enable Preferred pin with strict thresholds for 10 internal customers. Collect telemetry for 48–72 hours.
3) Expand progressively, exposing per-customer opt-out toggle on console.

Open questions / risks (to resolve before rollout):
- How do we measure "quality delta" for arbitrary models? Need a small evaluative prompt set per model family (product-build) and a quality threshold.
- Who can change compatibility metadata? Changing op_vector/quantization after pin could silently break strict guarantees. Need a registry write-protection policy for pinned artifacts.
- Latency of registry updates vs router caches: define TTLs and automatic invalidation on metadata changes.
- Billing/chargeback: if fallback routes to more expensive variant, how to bill customer? Prefer to bill at chosen-variant rate and note in invoice.

Operational playbook sketch (short):
- Detection: dashboard alerts when fallback rate > 0.5% for a customer OR average latency increase > 20% for pinned routes.
- Mitigation: 1) Throttle new requests, 2) Promote missing artifact to region (deploy job), 3) Temporarily increase capacity in Dedicated pools, 4) Revert routing policy to strict for affected customer.
- Post-mortem: include link to replay data, list of fallbacks, and metric deltas.

Next steps / TODOs (owner-assigned):
- [Priya] Build simulation harness to replay routing choices (due 2025-02-28).
- [Ethan] Add small compatibility vector API prototype to registry (draft PR linked).
- [Luis] Define evaluation prompt sets for top-10 most-used models (help coordinate with Applied ML).
- [Marta] Draft console UI copy for fallback notifications and per-customer pin policy.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Might be worth exploring a tiny ML model in control plane that predicts quality delta of a quantized variant given prompt-length distribution + few-shot examples. Heavy lift but could reduce manual thresholds.
- For Dedicated/private fleets we should surface an "allow_relaxed_pinning" toggle in tenant config; default off.

References and links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/registry/pull/412 (compat vector prototype)
- Jira: JIRA-PLAT-789 (pinning telemetry epic)
- Slack thread: slack://channel/platform-telemetry/thread/abcd1234

End of exploratory notes — feedback welcome. Will convert to a formal proposal if team agrees on scoring primitives and simulation results look safe.

-- Priya
